identity.what_it_is: A small, west-facing, no-take marine-reserve beach at Manly, Sydney, part of Cabbage Tree Bay Aquatic Reserve; popular for snorkelling, scuba diving and swimming.
identity.where: Manly, a suburb of Sydney, New South Wales, Australia, adjacent to North Head and Fairy Bower.
identity.warnings: Australia has at least six other places called Shelly Beach (Central Coast NSW, Cronulla NSW, Sunshine Coast QLD, Townsville QLD, plus one in New Zealand and one in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa) per the Wikipedia disambiguation page (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shelly_Beach) — do not let facts about those leak in. Shelly Beach (Cronulla) is a distinct, unrelated ~40m beach on Bate Bay. Scout notes also flag an unresolved Wikidata QID mismatch (Q7493888 vs Q21957501) for this beach that no harvested source resolves — unverified, needs a direct Wikidata check before publishing.

spike_candidates.statement: A 1920s scheme to turn Shelly Beach into an amusement park was defeated by locals; the site became a 20ha no-take marine reserve in 2002.
spike_candidates.tension: The pristine snorkelling reserve tourists photograph today exists only because residents blocked a Coney-Island-style redevelopment a century earlier.

spike_candidates.statement: A swimmer was seriously injured in a suspected shark attack between Manly and Shelly Beach in 2019, and a bull shark killed a dolphin there in 2023.
spike_candidates.tension: Marketing copy calling the reserve safe for casual swimmers and snorkellers sits next to two real, recent, serious shark encounters in the same water.

spike_candidates.statement: Sydney's 2025 Beachwatch report placed Shelly Beach's water quality among the city's ten worst swim sites, with bacteria levels nearly double the safe limit.
spike_candidates.tension: "Smelly Shelly" undercuts the beach's image as a jewel of the marine reserve — the same water prized for snorkelling regularly breaches safe-swimming thresholds after rain.

facts.fact: Shelly Beach (also called Shelley Beach) is a beach in Manly, a Sydney suburb, adjacent to North Head and Fairy Bower.
facts.quote: shelly beach (also known as shelley beach) [ 1 ] is a beach located in manly , a suburb of sydney , new south wales , australia . it is adjacent to north head and fairy bower .
facts.source_title: Shelly Beach (Manly) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Wikipedia describes Shelly Beach as a reflective beach about 100 metres long.
facts.quote: shelly beach is a reflective beach about 100 metres long.
facts.source_title: Shelly Beach (Manly) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The beach is shallow, with a maximum depth around 12 metres and most areas 2-6 metres deep, making it popular with snorkellers.
facts.quote: its maximum depth being about 12 metres. many areas are shallow with depths ranging from 2 to 6 metres.
facts.source_title: Shelly Beach (Manly) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Cabbage Tree Bay, which includes Shelly Beach, was declared a 'no take' aquatic reserve on 31 March 2002.
facts.quote: cabbage tree bay was declared a 'no take' aquatic reserve on 31 march 2002.
facts.source_title: Shelly Beach (Manly) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The Cabbage Tree Bay Aquatic Reserve infobox lists its area as 17 hectares, established 31 March 2002 and managed by the NSW Department of Primary Industries.
facts.quote: area 17 ha (42 acres) established 31 march 2002
facts.source_title: Cabbage Tree Bay Aquatic Reserve - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The beach's name comes from a shell midden recorded near the Fairy Bower car park, even though the beach itself is not especially shelly.
facts.quote: this is the reason for its name even though the beach itself is not that shelly.
facts.source_title: Shelly Beach (Manly) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: A severe storm on 4-5 June 2016 badly damaged the walkway between Manly Beach and Shelly Beach, including the sculpture at Fairy Bower Pool.
facts.quote: on the weekend of june 4 & 5, 2016 a severe storm caused extensive damage to the walkway between manly beach and shelly beach.
facts.source_title: Shelly Beach (Manly) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Safety barriers installed after the 2016 storm were removed in August 2016 once remediation work was complete.
facts.quote: the barriers were removed in august 2016, following the completion of remediation work.
facts.source_title: Shelly Beach (Manly) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Over 160 species of fish and about 50 species of marine invertebrates have been recorded in Cabbage Tree Bay Aquatic Reserve.
facts.quote: over 160 different species of fish and about 50 species of marine invertebrates have been reported in the marine reserve.
facts.source_title: Cabbage Tree Bay Aquatic Reserve - Wikipedia

facts.fact: A small colony of the hard coral Pocillopora aliciae, normally a tropical species, has established in the bay as its range shifts with warming seas.
facts.quote: a small colony of hard corals of the species pocillopora aliciae was also found in the bay.
facts.source_title: Cabbage Tree Bay Aquatic Reserve - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The reserve's Eastern blue groper is a sequential hermaphrodite: females are brown to reddish-brown, and the largest turn male (and blue) when no males are present.
facts.quote: the females are brown to reddish-brown, larger ones turn into males, especially when there are no males in a group, and acquire a strong blue colour.
facts.source_title: Cabbage Tree Bay Aquatic Reserve - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Shelly Beach has two free electric barbecues, showers, toilets and a kiosk, plus a bush track around the headland.
facts.quote: facilities include 2 free electric barbecues, showers, toilets and a kiosk selling meals, drinks and coffee.
facts.source_title: Shelly Beach (Manly) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The Boathouse Shelly Beach restaurant operates on the beach itself.
facts.quote: there is a restaurant on the beach called the boathouse shelly beach.
facts.source_title: Shelly Beach (Manly) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Parking at Shelly Beach's facilities is charged at $8.00 an hour.
facts.quote: the facilities also include parking at the rate of $8.00 an hour.
facts.source_title: Shelly Beach (Manly) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Many scuba diving centres take beginner students to Shelly Beach because conditions are excellent for learning to dive.
facts.quote: many scuba diving centres take students because it offers excellent conditions for an environment in which to learn scuba.
facts.source_title: Shelly Beach (Manly) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The opening scene of the 1983 film BMX Bandits was shot on the walkway between Manly Beach and Shelly Beach.
facts.quote: in the opening scene of the 1983 film bmx bandits , two characters ride their bicycles down the walkway between manly beach and shelly beach .
facts.source_title: Shelly Beach (Manly) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The western point of the beach has a surf break called 'Bower', one of Sydney's most shallow-breaking waves; Winki and Deadman's breaks lie further along.
facts.quote: on the western point of the beach is a surf break known as "bower" which offers one of the most shallow breaking waves in sydney.
facts.source_title: Shelly Beach (Manly) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The rocky shore of Cabbage Tree Bay was already an intertidal protected area from 1993 before the full marine park was designated in 2002.
facts.quote: the rocky shore of cabbage tree bay was designated an intertidal protected area from 1993 to 2002.
facts.source_title: Cabbage Tree Bay Aquatic Reserve - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The reserve packs sandy beach, rocky shore, reefs, seagrass meadows and kelp forest habitats into a small area.
facts.quote: the cabbage tree bay aquatic reserve encompasses various habitats in a small area, with a sandy beach to the east, a rocky shore to the south, and reefs, seagrass meadows, and kelp forests.
facts.source_title: Cabbage Tree Bay Aquatic Reserve - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The reserve covers roughly 20 hectares, spanning the whole bay, rocky shores and beaches from the south end of Manly Beach to the north end of Shelly Beach headland.
facts.quote: it covers an area of approximately 20 hectares, including the entire bay, rocky shores and beaches from the southern end of manly beach to the northern end of shelly beach headland.
facts.source_title: Cabbage Tree Bay Aquatic Reserve Map | NSW Department of Primary Industries

facts.fact: A popular fishing spot called 'Blueys', at the southeast end of the Shelly Beach headland car park, sits outside the no-take reserve boundary within the separate intertidal protected area, where line fishing is allowed but collecting invertebrates is not.
facts.quote: a popular recreational fishing site at the south eastern end of the car park on shelly beach headland, known as blueys, is not within the boundaries of the aquatic reserve but is within shelly beach headland intertidal protected area where you can go line fishing but collecting marine invertebrates is prohibited.
facts.source_title: Cabbage Tree Bay Aquatic Reserve Map | NSW Department of Primary Industries

facts.fact: NSW DPI calls Shelly Beach the only west-facing beach on the NSW coast, making it a spot to watch the sunset after swimming or diving.
facts.quote: shelly beach is the only west facing beach on the nsw coast and this makes it a great spot to watch the sun set after a day of swimming, snorkelling or scuba diving.
facts.source_title: Cabbage Tree Bay Aquatic Reserve Map | NSW Department of Primary Industries

facts.fact: NSW DPI's current page names the Gayamaygal people of the Eora nation as the traditional custodians of the Cabbage Tree Bay area.
facts.quote: the traditional custodians of this area are the gayamaygal people of the eora nation.
facts.source_title: Cabbage Tree Bay Aquatic Reserve | NSW Department of Primary Industries

facts.fact: Cabbage Tree Bay was declared a no-take aquatic reserve in March 2002, per Northern Beaches Council.
facts.quote: cabbage tree bay was declared a no take aquatic reserve in march 2002.
facts.source_title: Cabbage Tree Bay Aquatic Reserve | Northern Beaches Council

facts.fact: Dogs are prohibited from the aquatic reserve and beach area at all times.
facts.quote: dogs are prohibited from entering the aquatic reserve and beach area at all times.
facts.source_title: Cabbage Tree Bay Aquatic Reserve | Northern Beaches Council

facts.fact: Shelly Beach's council status page states the beach is not patrolled by lifeguards.
facts.quote: this beach is not patrolled by lifeguards
facts.source_title: Shelly Beach | Northern Beaches Council

facts.fact: Weddings at Shelly Beach are permitted only between May and October.
facts.quote: weddings at shelly beach are permitted between the months of may and october.
facts.source_title: Shelly Beach | Northern Beaches Council

facts.fact: A resident green turtle nicknamed Basil is a local celebrity at Shelly Beach, regularly seen grazing on seagrass.
facts.quote: basil the green turtle munching on seagrass.
facts.source_title: Dive into the history of Cabbage Tree Bay, Manly - History Matters

facts.fact: Developers proposed converting the Manly/Shelly Beach area into an amusement park in the 1920s; local community opposition got the plans terminated, paving the way for the later no-take reserve.
facts.quote: there were once proposals to completely revamp the scenery at manly a century ago in the 1920s.
facts.source_title: Dive into the history of Cabbage Tree Bay, Manly - History Matters

facts.fact: Community lobbying against the 1920s amusement scheme is credited with Cabbage Tree Bay eventually becoming a no-take aquatic reserve.
facts.quote: luckily thanks to the local community effort, not only were the plans terminated, but cabbage tree bay also became a no-take aquatic reserve.
facts.source_title: Dive into the history of Cabbage Tree Bay, Manly - History Matters

facts.fact: Dive Centre Manly has served the local community from Belgrave Street since 1962.
facts.quote: dive centre manly , a local dive centre that has been serving the manly community at belgrave street since 1962
facts.source_title: Dive into the history of Cabbage Tree Bay, Manly - History Matters

facts.fact: Manly's Shelly Beach ranked among Sydney's ten worst swim sites in the 2025 State of the Beaches report, based on pollution samples from October 2024 to October 2025.
facts.quote: manly's shelly beach has landed among the bottom ten swim sites in sydney in this year's annual report on water quality results, examining real pollution samples from october 2024 to october 2025.
facts.source_title: Smelly Shelly takes the shine off, but Northern Beaches dominate with clean water testing - Manly Observer

facts.fact: Shelly Beach's mean enterococci reading was 79.4 CFU/100mL, nearly double the safe swimming limit.
facts.quote: at shelly beach, the average (mean) reading was 79.4 cfu/100ml, nearly double the safe limit.
facts.source_title: Smelly Shelly takes the shine off, but Northern Beaches dominate with clean water testing - Manly Observer

facts.fact: NSW's Beachwatch program monitors 249 swim sites statewide for enterococci bacteria as an indicator of faecal contamination.
facts.quote: the state's beachwatch program monitors water quality at 249 swim sites across nsw, measuring levels of enterococci bacteria.
facts.source_title: Smelly Shelly takes the shine off, but Northern Beaches dominate with clean water testing - Manly Observer

facts.fact: NHMRC guidance holds water safe for swimming when enterococci stay below 41 CFU per 100mL.
facts.quote: water is considered safe for swimming when enterococci levels remain below 41 colony-forming units (cfu) per 100 millilitres.
facts.source_title: Smelly Shelly takes the shine off, but Northern Beaches dominate with clean water testing - Manly Observer

facts.fact: Statewide, 76% of NSW swim sites were graded good or very good in the 2025 report, an improvement on the prior year.
facts.quote: statewide, the report found 76% of swim sites were graded good or very good, meaning they were suitable for swimming most or all of the time.
facts.source_title: Smelly Shelly takes the shine off, but Northern Beaches dominate with clean water testing - Manly Observer

facts.fact: Ocean beaches performed particularly well in 2025, with 95% rated good or very good.
facts.quote: ocean beaches performed particularly well, with 95% rated good or very good in 2025
facts.source_title: Smelly Shelly takes the shine off, but Northern Beaches dominate with clean water testing - Manly Observer

facts.fact: On 21 January 2023 a dolphin died after being mauled by a suspected bull shark near Shelly Beach, suspending the Manly Open Surf Carnival.
facts.quote: a dolphin has died after it was mauled by at least one suspected bull shark on sydney's northern beaches, suspending the manly open surf carnival.
facts.source_title: Surf carnival suspended after dolphin attacked by shark in Sydney's north - ABC News

facts.fact: Three bull sharks were spotted near Shelly Beach in Manly at the time of the January 2023 dolphin attack.
facts.quote: three bull sharks were spotted near shelly beach in manly, where the attack occurred this morning, according to surf lifesaving nsw.
facts.source_title: Surf carnival suspended after dolphin attacked by shark in Sydney's north - ABC News

facts.fact: Beaches between Shelly Beach and Queenscliff were closed as a precaution and monitored after the 2023 shark sighting.
facts.quote: beaches between shelley and queenscliff have been closed as a precaution and are being monitored for further shark sightings.
facts.source_title: Surf carnival suspended after dolphin attacked by shark in Sydney's north - ABC News

facts.fact: On 2 July 2019, Manly resident Peter Schultz, 57, was attacked by a suspected shark while swimming between Manly and Shelly Beaches before dawn, suffering serious cuts to his leg, abdomen and hand.
facts.quote: manly resident peter schultz was swimming with a small group of people between sydney's manly and shelly beaches before dawn on tuesday morning. the 57 year-old was attacked by what is suspected to have been a shark, receiving serious cuts to his leg, abdomen and hand.
facts.source_title: Man attacked by shark at Sydney's Manly Beach - Surf Life Saving NSW

facts.fact: After the 2019 attack, Manly Beach was closed by council lifeguards for 24 hours; there had been five shark attacks or major encounters in NSW in the preceding 12 months.
facts.quote: manly beach has been closed by northern beaches council lifeguards for 24 hours. there have been five shark attacks or major encounters in nsw in the last 12 months.
facts.source_title: Man attacked by shark at Sydney's Manly Beach - Surf Life Saving NSW

facts.fact: A NSW Department of Education teaching resource also calls Shelly Beach's reserve the only west-facing aquatic reserve on Australia's east coast.
facts.quote: it is the only west-facing aquatic reserve on australia's east coast.
facts.source_title: Shelly Beach - Manly Through Time

facts.fact: A 2001 Manly Council heritage-walk guide names the Kayimai and Cannalgal people as the traditional owners of the Manly/Shelly Beach area, differing in wording from NSW DPI's current 'Gayamaygal' framing.
facts.quote: the kayimai and cannalgal people of this area
facts.source_title: Eastern Hill Heritage Walk - Manly & Northern Beaches Australia

facts.fact: Cabbage Tree Bay was once an important commercial fishing ground; up to fifty years ago huge schools of kingfish, salmon and tuna were netted there.
facts.quote: cabbage tree bay was once an important commercial fishing area in nsw. up to fifty years ago, huge schools of kingfish, salmon and tuna were netted here.
facts.source_title: Eastern Hill Heritage Walk - Manly & Northern Beaches Australia

facts.fact: A 1998 Ministry for Fisheries/University of Sydney marine study found a rich diversity of fish in Cabbage Tree Bay, including four protected species and the blue groper.
facts.quote: in 1998 the ministry for fisheries launched a marine study conducted by the university of sydney which found a rich diversity of fish, including four protected species and the blue groper.
facts.source_title: Eastern Hill Heritage Walk - Manly & Northern Beaches Australia

facts.fact: Shelly Beach was named for the huge quantities of shells once deposited by the tide; by 1933 hundreds had been taken and few remain today.
facts.quote: this beach is named for the enormous quantity of shells that used to be found here. in the 1920s the tide regularly deposited shells. by 1933 it was reported that hundreds of shells had been taken from the beach.
facts.source_title: Eastern Hill Heritage Walk - Manly & Northern Beaches Australia

facts.fact: The Sly family kept fishing boats at Shelly Beach from 1888 and by 1903 were patrolling with their boat, demonstrating early surf rescue methods.
facts.quote: the sly family kept fishing boats here from 1888, and in 1903 patrolled with their boat, demonstrating surf rescue methods.
facts.source_title: Eastern Hill Heritage Walk - Manly & Northern Beaches Australia

facts.fact: In 1936, G.J. Sly found an extremely rare vampire octopus washed up at Shelly Beach - one of only ten ever sighted worldwide and the only one found in Australia - which ended up used as bait.
facts.quote: in 1936 g. j. sly found an extremely rare vampire octopus washed up here, one of only ten sighted throughout the world and the only one ever found in australia. it was about 1.25 metres across and pink in colour, and it ended its life ignominiously as bait.
facts.source_title: Eastern Hill Heritage Walk - Manly & Northern Beaches Australia

facts.fact: Shelly Beach's present stone kiosk began life as a tearoom built in 1923, hosting community dances in the 1920s.
facts.quote: the present stone kiosk was originally a tearoom when it was built in 1923.
facts.source_title: Eastern Hill Heritage Walk - Manly & Northern Beaches Australia

facts.fact: Shelly Beach and its ocean foreshore, after being excluded from public access in 1885, were returned to the public in 1898 at Manly Council's request.
facts.quote: it was not until 1898 that shelly beach and the ocean foreshore were returned to the people at manly council's request, as this was such a popular recreation place.
facts.source_title: Eastern Hill Heritage Walk - Manly & Northern Beaches Australia

facts.fact: After St Patrick's College's 1885 cornerstone-laying ceremony, the assembled crowd descended to Shelly Beach for lunch in a marquee.
facts.quote: after the ceremony everyone descended to shelly beach for lunch in a marquee.
facts.source_title: Eastern Hill Heritage Walk - Manly & Northern Beaches Australia

facts.fact: Of the Eastern Hill Heritage Walk's three sections, only the South Steyne-to-Shelly Beach leg is fully wheelchair accessible.
facts.quote: only the section south steyne to shelly beach and return is fully accessible to wheelchairs.
facts.source_title: Eastern Hill Heritage Walk - Manly & Northern Beaches Australia

facts.fact: Public toilets on this stretch of coast are at Little Manly Beach, Shelly Beach and Fairy Bower.
facts.quote: there are toilets at little manly beach, shelly beach and fairy bower.
facts.source_title: Eastern Hill Heritage Walk - Manly & Northern Beaches Australia

facts.fact: Manly Beach connects to Fairy Bower and Shelly Beach via a walking oceanway, within walking distance of Manly's shops and restaurants.
facts.quote: within walking distance of manly beach along the oceanway is fairy bower and shelly beach.
facts.source_title: Manly Beach - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Northern Beaches Council lifeguards run a year-round service at South Steyne (Manly Beach) and a seasonal (October-April) service further along at North Steyne and Queenscliff.
facts.quote: northern beaches council lifeguards operate a year-round service at south steyne, and operate from october to april at north steyne and queenscliff.
facts.source_title: Manly Beach - Wikipedia

conflicts: Reserve area: Wikipedia's Cabbage Tree Bay Aquatic Reserve infobox states 17 hectares (F05), while NSW DPI (F20, F23) and Northern Beaches Council (F24) both state approximately 20 hectares.

Traditional custodians: NSW DPI's current page names the Gayamaygal people of the Eora nation (F23), while the 2001 Manly Council heritage-walk guide names the Kayimai and Cannalgal people (F44) - wording differs across official and historical sources.

Spelling/place-name: the ABC's 2023 shark-incident report refers to 'beaches between shelley and queenscliff' (F40), an older spelling variant of Shelly, consistent with Wikipedia noting 'Shelley Beach' as an alias (F01).
